test_title: SSC MTS 2024 Official Paper (Held On: 29 Oct, 2024 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: The diameter of a hollow hemisphere is 30 cm. Water is filled in it up to its brim. When spherical lead shots each of radius 0.75 cm are dropped into the hemisphere, two-fifth of the water flows out. How many lead shots were dropped into the hemisphere?
solution:
**Given:**

Radius of the hollow hemisphere (R) = 30 / 2 = 15 cm

Radius of each lead shot (r) = 0.75 cm

Two-fifth of the water flows out

**Formula used:**

Volume of hemisphere = (2/3) × π × R³

Volume of a sphere = (4/3) × π × r³

Number of lead shots = (Volume of water displaced) / (Volume of 1 lead shot)

**Calculations:**

Volume of hemisphere = (2/3) × π × R³

⇒ Volume of hemisphere = (2/3) × π × (15)³

Water displaced = (2/5) × Volume of hemisphere

⇒ Water displaced = (2/5) × (2/3) × π × (15)3

Volume of 1 lead shot = (4/3) × π × r³

⇒ Volume of 1 lead shot = (4/3) × π × (0.75)³

Number of lead shots = Water displaced / Volume of 1 lead shot

⇒ Number of lead shots = [(2/5) × (2/3) × π × (15)3] / [(4/3) × π × (0.75)3]

⇒ Number of lead shots = 1/5 × (15 / 0.75)³ = 1/5 × (20)³ = 1600

**∴ The correct answer is option (3).**
